title: Networking, API design, DNS/LB/CDN
summary: The request path (DNS, TLS, HTTP versions, pooling, L4/L7 load balancing, health checks, CDNs), API design (errors, pagination, versioning, REST/gRPC/GraphQL, webhooks), and idempotency + auth for money-moving APIs.

labs.title: Load balancer: pickers (RR, least-conn, P2C), passive ejection, draining, reverse proxy
Keyset pagination with HMAC-signed cursors vs offset
Idempotency-Key middleware: atomic reservation, replay, leases
HMAC-signed JWT-style tokens with kid rotation and strict alg checks

outcomes.text: Estimate the latency cost of the request path in round trips (TCP, TLS 1.2/1.3, QUIC, keep-alive vs new connections) and explain why DNS failover is slow.
Diagnose connection-reuse bugs in Go HTTP clients and size connection pools with Little's law.
Choose between L4 and L7 load balancing and between round robin, least-connections and power-of-two-choices, and explain when the answer flips.
Implement a load balancer with pluggable pickers, passive outlier ejection with probation, and connection draining.
Decide what a CDN may cache in an authenticated banking app and how to deploy behind it safely.
Design resource-oriented APIs with correct method semantics, status codes, an error model and evolution rules; choose between REST, gRPC and GraphQL.
Implement keyset pagination with HMAC-signed opaque cursors and explain why offset pagination duplicates and skips rows under concurrent writes.
Design long-running operations and webhooks that survive at-least-once, unordered delivery.
Implement idempotency-key middleware that executes once under concurrent duplicates, and defend its design choices.
Choose authentication and authorisation mechanisms (sessions vs JWT, OAuth code + PKCE, client credentials, OIDC, SAML, mTLS, API keys) and where tokens are validated.
Implement a JWT-compatible HMAC token verifier with kid rotation, leeway and strict algorithm checks.
